# gatekeep-pr #42: cap re-entry, independent cases B, C and D

## Main case: re-entry at the cap, then one `deliver` pick

### Re-entry state

- **Tracker.** I init no new stages. The original run initialized `gather, provision, verify`, with no `sync` stage because `--rebase` was not passed. On this re-entry I `add` only `report` and then `menu` as each starts.
- **Assessed head.** Verification and the brief assess `1111111111111111111111111111111111111111`. The evidence is `source: ci`, run 910 (`ci / test` SUCCESS) on that exact head.

### Commands, in order

1. **Validate the run record.**
   - I read `/tmp/gatekeep-state.synthetic`.
   - I match `consent.target` (`acme/widgets`, `42`, `main`) against the base repository, PR number and live `baseRefName`. All three match.
   - Course is `deliver`. Accounting is `rounds 10/10`, `syncs 10/10`.
2. **Check the stored wave.** The last helper result has no `open - needs` reason and there is no no-progress checkpoint, so no early exit applies.
3. **Pre-menu refresh, read-only.**
   - `gh pr view 42 --json headRefOid,state,mergeable,mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision,statusCheckRollup,body,baseRefName,number,title,author,isDraft,headRefName,isCrossRepository,files,additions,deletions,commits,reviews,closingIssuesReferences,headRepository,maintainerCanModify,url,mergeCommit`
   - `gh run list -R acme/widgets -c 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111 --json databaseId,status,conclusion,workflowName,url`
   - Results: head, body and base are unchanged, `mergeStateStatus: BEHIND`, `ci / test` is green, and no check is pending.
4. **Exit check.**
   - Readiness fails because P1 is open and the branch is BEHIND.
   - The obstacle table only routes BEHIND and the repairable gap back into the course.
   - The cap row matches first: `round cap reached: 10 of 10`. The sync cap is also exhausted at 10 of 10.
   - I render the obstacle template and keep the local state as is.

### Report

There is no `Sync:` line: `--rebase` was not passed.

```
Delivers: the event guard rejects unsigned events.

PR comments:
- GitHub reports the branch is behind main, so merge waits until the next sync. (merge_state_status BEHIND)

Blockers:
1. An unsigned event wrapped in an array passes the guard, so an attacker can still deliver unsigned events. (src/guard.mjs)

Evidence: CI (run 910, ci / test green on 1111111)
Verdict: not ready - round cap reached: 10 of 10

Pick one:
1. deliver - resume the retained course; repair the array bypass and sync onto main, no round charged; add 10 to each cap (+2 x 5: rounds 10 of 20, syncs 10 of 20).
2. assess - switch course; post the open blocker as a review, no repairs.
3. stop - remove the worktree, leave the PR as is. [recommended]

Type a number; show evidence prints the full record (CI run 910, ci / test green on 1111111).
```

### Pick and persistence

The human types `1`, which maps to `deliver`. Before any work I persist:
- course `deliver`
- `repair.rounds_cap: 20`, `repair.syncs_cap: 20`
- `rounds_used: 10`, `syncs_used: 10`, unchanged

Narration stops here, with no helper dispatched.

### How the recorded usage was charged

- **Rounds.** Each of the ten rounds is one counted wave that left a new source-changing commit. This includes the mixed wave, which was charged one round.
- **Syncs.** The ten syncs are loop syncs, one each. They cover:
  - the conflict-only syncs, which cost a sync but no round
  - the sync inside the mixed wave, which cost one sync on top of its one round
- **Description-only writes** cost nothing.
- **The extension** adds exactly `2 x maxFixRounds` = 10 to each cap. Usage is never reset.

## Independent B: runtime fix-round guard refuses the dispatch

**Starting state:** caps 20/20, usage 10/10, course `deliver`.

1. I validate the record and run the pre-menu refresh, the same two reads as above. Nothing has changed.
2. Exit check finds no exit, since 10 < 20.
3. D3 step 1 starts the wave:
   - `git -C /work/widgets-pr-42 rev-parse HEAD` records `pre_wave_head` = `1111111`.
   - `git -C /work/widgets-pr-42 fetch origin main`
   - `git -C /work/widgets-pr-42 merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` exits 0.
4. I attempt to dispatch the `implementer` (fresh, sync, cwd `/work/widgets-pr-42`). It would carry:
   - the P1 evidence pack
   - `SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS = node --test src/guard.test.mjs`
   - the commit-only-on-green and discard-on-red rules
5. The runtime refuses: `closureReview.enforce: maximum fix rounds reached`. Nothing is dispatched, no commit is made, and no round is charged. Usage stays 10/10 against caps 20/20.

```
Delivers: the event guard rejects unsigned events.

PR comments:
- GitHub reports the branch is behind main, so merge waits until the next sync. (merge_state_status BEHIND)

Blockers:
1. An unsigned event wrapped in an array passes the guard, so an attacker can still deliver unsigned events. (src/guard.mjs)

Evidence: CI (run 910, ci / test green on 1111111)
Verdict: not ready - stuck - phase-tracker fix-round guard: closureReview.enforce: maximum fix rounds reached

Pick one:
1. deliver - resume the retained course; retries the array-bypass repair only once the runtime fix-round guard permits, no round charged; add 10 to each cap (+2 x 5: rounds 10 of 30, syncs 10 of 30).
2. assess - switch course; post the open blocker as a review, no repairs.
3. stop - remove the worktree, leave the PR as is. [recommended]

Type a number; show evidence prints the full record (CI run 910, ci / test green on 1111111).
```

## Independent C: unchanged no-progress checkpoint

**Starting state:** caps 20/20, usage 10/10, and `repair.wave.no_progress` is set.

1. I validate the record.
2. The early exit fires immediately, before any watch or dispatch:
   - The failed input is unchanged: same source, same test, same command `node --test src/guard.test.mjs`.
   - The helper result at `/tmp/guard-failed.synthetic` shows edits restored and no commit.
   - The verdict is `stuck - no progress: node --test src/guard.test.mjs: constant-time comparison`.
3. I run the pre-menu refresh, which changes nothing. I dispatch no helper and leave course and counters intact at 10/20 rounds and 10/20 syncs.

```

2. assess - switch course; post the open blocker as a review, no repairs.

Type a number; show evidence prints the full record (CI run 910, ci / test green on 1111111).

## Independent D: held workflow run the viewer cannot approve

**Starting state:** course `deliver`, `rounds 2/10`, `syncs 1/10`.

1. I validate the record.
2. I run the pre-menu refresh, the same `gh pr view` and `gh run list` reads.
3. Exit check matches the `action_required` row: the viewer cannot approve the held run. The verdict is `stuck - workflow run awaiting approval`, so no `approve workflow run` row renders.

```

1. An unsigned event wrapped in an array passes the guard, so an attacker can still deliver unsigned events. (src/guard.mjs)

Evidence: pending (held workflow run binding; head 1111111)
Verdict: not ready - stuck - workflow run awaiting approval

Pick one:
1. deliver - resume the retained course; retries once the held run is approved, no round charged; add 10 to each cap (+2 x 5: rounds 2 of 20, syncs 1 of 20).
2. assess - switch course; post the open blocker as a review, no repairs.

Not offered: approve workflow run (viewer cannot approve the held run)
Type a number; show evidence prints the full record (pending, held workflow run binding on 1111111).

The human clears the held run outside the gate and types `1`, which maps to `deliver`. Before any work I persist:
- course `deliver`

```bash

```

3. The runtime refuses the dispatch with `closureReview.enforce: maximum fix rounds reached`. No helper executes, no commit is created, and no round or sync is charged. I do not retry through another persona or bypass the guard.
